Measuring peanut butter

Peanut butter is dense. A cup weighs about 256 g, which you can check against any jar: the nutrition label lists a serving as 2 tablespoons, or 32 g. Smooth and crunchy weigh almost the same. Natural peanut butter with the oil stirred in weighs slightly more.

Measuring sticky ingredients by the cup is messy and inaccurate, because a spoonful or more always stays stuck to the cup. Weighing straight into the bowl is quicker. A light coat of oil on the measuring cup also helps it slide out.

Source: US nutrition labels (2 tablespoons = 32 g); USDA FoodData Central lists 258 g per cup.

Questions

How many grams is ½ cup of peanut butter?

½ cup of peanut butter weighs about 128 g (4.52 oz). A full cup is 256 g.

How many cups is 100 grams of peanut butter?

100 g of peanut butter is about ⅜ cup, based on 256 g per cup.

How many grams is 2 tablespoons of peanut butter?

About 32 g. That's the standard serving size printed on US peanut butter labels, and it works out to 256 g per cup.
